app.name: Smartsheet
app.summary: OAuth access lets an agent read and modify a user's Smartsheet sheets, rows, reports, dashboards and workspaces, limited to the scopes the user grants.

verdict.headline: No app review, but only a licensed Business-plan (or higher) Smartsheet user can register as a developer.

rationale.text: The public Developer Tools Registration page says the registering email must belong to an existing licensed Smartsheet user on a Business plan or higher, and that you agree to the Smartsheet Developer Agreement. Third-party setup guides say Smartsheet then activates Developer Tools for that account once it approves the request. After that you create a developer profile and an app in Developer Tools, and you get the client ID and secret straight away. No source we read describes a review before other Smartsheet users can authorize an app. The 'Publish App?' option seems to affect only whether the app is listed publicly. The paid-plan requirement and the activation wait are the only gates.

effort.approvalWait: None to a few days (Developer Tools activation; no published timeline)
effort.firstConnection: Same day once Developer Tools is activated

basis.text: Smartsheet does not say how long Developer Tools activation takes. Third-party guides only say Smartsheet activates it after approving the request. The 0-3 day estimate is an inference. App creation itself is a single form that returns credentials straight away.

stages.name: Developer Tools activated on a Business+ account
stages.whoCanConnect: Nobody yet. You only have the ability to create apps.

limit.text: You register a licensed Business-plan (or higher) user's email at developers.smartsheet.com/register and accept the Developer Agreement. Smartsheet then activates Developer Tools for that account. Free accounts cannot register OAuth apps.

stages.name: App created, test with your own account
stages.whoCanConnect: You and any Smartsheet user you send through the authorize URL

limit.text: Clicking Create New App and then Save returns the App client ID and App secret straight away. No source mentions a test-user allowlist or a cap on how many users can connect.

stages.name: Any customer can connect
stages.whoCanConnect: Any Smartsheet user whose plan and admin settings allow API/third-party app access

limit.text: No documented review step stands between your app and production use. Customers' own org admins or plan limits may still block third-party apps. This is inferred and was not confirmed in the docs we read.

steps.title: Choose a service Smartsheet account on Business plan or higher
steps.detail: Pick or buy a licensed Smartsheet seat on Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management. Smartsheet suggests using an email address that isn't tied to one person, so the app survives staff changes.
steps.doneWhen: You can log in to app.smartsheet.com as a licensed user on a Business+ plan

steps.title: Register for Developer Tools
steps.detail: On the Developer Tools Registration page, enter the account email, accept the Smartsheet Developer Agreement and click Register User Account. Then wait for Smartsheet to activate Developer Tools.
steps.doneWhen: A Developer Tools entry appears under the Account icon in Smartsheet

steps.title: Create Developer Profile
steps.detail: In Smartsheet, open Account icon → Developer Tools and click Create Developer Profile. Fill in the profile modal.
steps.doneWhen: The Developer Tools window shows a Create New App button

steps.title: Create New App
steps.detail: Click Create New App and fill in App Name, App Description (users see it on the consent screen, so make it polished), App URL, App Contact/Support, App Redirect URL (your Composio callback URL) and the 'Publish App?' toggle. Adding a logo is optional. An agent can draft the copy. Click Save.
steps.doneWhen: A confirmation window shows the App client ID and App secret

steps.title: Pick scopes and test the flow
steps.detail: Ask only for the scopes you need, for example READ_SHEETS, WRITE_SHEETS, CREATE_SHEETS, CREATE_SIGHTS, SHARE_SHEETS, ADMIN_WORKSPACES. The authorize endpoint is https://app.smartsheet.com/b/authorize and the token endpoint is https://api.smartsheet.com/2.0/token. Connect your own account end to end.
steps.doneWhen: An API call such as GET /2.0/users/me succeeds with the issued access token

requirements.text: The registering email must belong to an existing licensed Smartsheet user on a Business plan or higher. Free and Pro accounts cannot register OAuth apps.
You must accept the Smartsheet Developer Agreement when you register.
You need a public App URL, a support contact and an exact App Redirect URL for the app form.

nuances.text: The Developer Tools Registration page loads without logging in. It also says apps that call Smartsheet directly without user authorization don't need Developer Tools; they can use an API access token instead.
Smartsheet publishes no OAuth discovery metadata: /.well-known/openid-configuration on app.smartsheet.com returns 404. Configure the endpoints by hand.

Sending an unknown client_id to /b/authorize returned a 403 Forbidden after a redirect to /b/, with no descriptive OAuth error. A bad client ID or redirect URL can therefore look like a generic block.
Access tokens are short-lived (about 7 days, from memory) and come with a refresh token. Smartsheet also uses its own token-exchange details, so check that the token request matches the OAuth guide.
Smartsheet runs separate regional instances (EU at smartsheet.eu, Smartsheetgov). These have different hosts and probably need a separate app registration. A US app won't authorize EU-region users.
Registering through some older flows created a new, separate Smartsheet account. Use the email of the licensed account you intend to manage the app from.

blockers.title: Account is not on a Business+ plan
blockers.signal: The Developer Tools menu never appears, or registration is refused, because the email isn't a licensed user on Business or higher
blockers.nextMove: Upgrade the service account, or register with a licensed seat in your company's Business/Enterprise org

blockers.title: Developer Tools activation pending
blockers.signal: You registered, but Account → Developer Tools isn't visible yet
blockers.nextMove: Wait for Smartsheet to activate it. If it takes more than a few days, contact Smartsheet Support

blockers.title: Redirect URL mismatch
blockers.signal: The authorize step fails, or returns a 403 or an error instead of the consent screen
blockers.nextMove: Make the App Redirect URL in Developer Tools exactly match the callback URL you use

agentCan: Draft the App Name, App Description (shown on the consent screen) and support contact text
Choose the minimal Smartsheet scopes (READ_SHEETS, WRITE_SHEETS, etc.) for the agent's features
Configure the authorize and token endpoints and test the OAuth flow end to end
Check that tokens refresh before they expire
youMust: Provide or buy a licensed Business-plan (or higher) Smartsheet seat, because a free account cannot register apps
Accept the Smartsheet Developer Agreement, which is a legal term
Log in to Smartsheet to create the developer profile and the app, and copy the client secret, because both happen in the logged-in UI

uncertainties.question: How long does Developer Tools activation take, and is it a manual approval?
uncertainties.howToResolve: Register and time it, or ask Smartsheet Support

uncertainties.question: What exactly does the 'Publish App?' toggle do, and does it trigger any review?
uncertainties.howToResolve: Read the toggle's help text in the Create New App form, or ask Smartsheet developer support

uncertainties.question: What is the current access-token lifetime and refresh-token behaviour?
uncertainties.howToResolve: Check the 'Get an access token' section of the OAuth guide, or look at expires_in in a test token response

uncertainties.question: Do EU and Gov-region users need a separately registered app on smartsheet.eu or smartsheetgov.com?
uncertainties.howToResolve: Check the Smartsheet API docs on regional base URLs and test with an EU account

uncertainties.question: Can customer org admins block third-party OAuth apps, or do customer plans restrict API access?
uncertainties.howToResolve: Check Smartsheet Help Center articles on admin controls for third-party integrations

providerContact.channel: Smartsheet Support (Help Center → Contact Support), or the Smartsheet Community API & Developers forum at community.smartsheet.com
providerContact.draftMessage: Hi, I registered <email> (Business plan) for Developer Tools on <date> to build an OAuth integration. Could you confirm (1) when Developer Tools will be activated, (2) whether the 'Publish App?' setting or anything else requires a review before users from other organizations can authorize our app, and (3) whether EU/Gov-region users need a separate app registration? Thanks.
